clinician.trajectory_summary: A 39-year-old nulliparous woman presented with a 2-year history of abnormal vaginal bleeding, weight loss, and an abdominal mass. Transabdominal ultrasonography revealed an 11.86×12.50×11.24 cm solid adnexal mass with normal uterus and liver, raising suspicion for ovarian carcinoma. Emergency laparotomy was performed, which demonstrated an enlarged uterus (16-18 weeks size), peritoneal seeding, and enlarged pelvic lymph nodes (2×3 cm right, 2×2 cm left). Histopathological examination of the surgical specimen confirmed the diagnosis of right ovarian malignant Brenner tumor with infiltration into the corpus uteri, lymphovascular invasion, and metastases to 2 right pelvic lymph nodes, 1 left pelvic lymph node, rectum, prevesical space, and Douglas pouch (pT2bN1bMx). Optimal cytoreductive surgery with R0 resection was achieved. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 3 and subsequently received adjuvant chemotherapy with paclitaxel (175 mg/m²) and carboplatin (6 AUC) every 21 days for 3 cycles. At 1-month follow-up after completion of adjuvant chemotherapy, the patient was recurrence-free with a normal CA-125 level.
